stdout:
usage: li [-h] [--version] [--machine]
          {orchestrate,o,agent,casts,engine,team,studio,schedule,state,invoke,kill,mirror,monitor,mon,dispatch,doctor,stats,plugin,hooks,handshake,runs,lifecycle,mcp}
          ...

lionagi command line — spawn subagents via any CLI-backed provider.

positional arguments:
  {orchestrate,o,agent,casts,engine,team,studio,schedule,state,invoke,kill,mirror,monitor,mon,dispatch,doctor,stats,plugin,hooks,handshake,runs,lifecycle,mcp}
    orchestrate (o)     Multi-agent orchestration patterns.
    agent               Spawn one-shot subagent (blocking); prints final
                        response.
    casts               inspect built-in roles and modes
    engine              Run domain-specific multi-agent engine pipelines.
    team                Team messaging — send/receive between named agents.
    studio              Lion Studio server
    schedule            Manage lionagi Studio schedules.
    state               Inspect and migrate lionagi state.db.
    invoke              Track a skill-level orchestration.
    kill                Terminate a running entity (run/session/play/show).
    mirror              Mirror Claude Code sessions into studio (live).
    monitor (mon)       Observe play/agent/run progress in real-time.
    dispatch            Inspect and acknowledge durable dispatch_outbox rows.
    doctor              Check the lionagi CLI environment/install for common
                        failure modes.
    stats               Read-only aggregate reporting over lionagi's StateDB.
    plugin              Inspect, trust, and enable/disable LionAGI plugin
                        bundles.
    hooks               Import Claude Code / Codex hook configs; trust
                        imported hook commands.
    handshake           Report the machine-result contract version this build
                        speaks.
    runs                List recorded runs and what each one wrote.
    lifecycle           Report the recorded lifecycle state of a run.
    mcp                 Serve the lionagi MCP server (background job
                        submit/query) over stdio.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --version             Print the installed lionagi version and exit.
  --machine             Emit one machine-result JSON object on stdout and send
                        every human-facing line to stderr.

stdout:
usage: li orchestrate flow [-h] [-f PATH] [-p NAME] [-a NAME]
                           [--with-synthesis [MODEL]]
                           [--max-concurrent MAX_CONCURRENT]
                           [--output {text,json}] [--save DIR]
                           [--team-mode [NAME]] [--team-attach NAME]
                           [--team-max-rounds N] [--dry-run] [--show-graph]
                           [--background] [--bare] [--workers M1,M2,...]
                           [--pack PATH] [--max-ops N] [--reactive MODE]
                           [--resume RUN_OR_SESSION_ID]
                           [--allow-degraded-context] [--mcp-config PATH]
                           [--no-mcp-config] [--yolo] [--bypass] [--fast] [-v]
                           [--theme {light,dark}] [--effort LEVEL] [--cwd DIR]
                           [--timeout SECONDS] [--invocation ID]
                           [--project NAME] [--resume-on-timeout]
                           [--notify CMD]
                           [[MODEL] PROMPT ...]

Orchestrator analyzes the task, composes a DAG of agents with dependency
edges, and executes with automatic parallelism where dependencies allow. Flags
may appear anywhere relative to the positionals.

positional arguments:
  [MODEL] PROMPT        Orchestrator model spec followed by the task prompt.
                        Model is optional when -a/--agent provides one; a
                        single positional is treated as the prompt. The prompt
                        itself may instead come from -f/--file or
                        -p/--playbook.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -f PATH, --file PATH  Load flow spec from YAML or JSON file. File values
                        serve as defaults; CLI flags override them. Prompt can
                        come from the file (prompt: key) or as a positional
                        argument.
  -p NAME, --playbook NAME
                        Load playbook from
                        ~/.lionagi/playbooks/<NAME>.playbook.yaml. Playbooks
                        may declare args: schema, artifacts: contracts, or
                        argument-hint: placeholders for prompt template
                        values.
  -a NAME, --agent NAME
                        Load orchestrator profile by name — resolves
                        .lionagi/agents/<NAME>/<NAME>.md first, then
                        .lionagi/agents/<NAME>.md.
  --with-synthesis [MODEL]
                        Run a final pass merging the DAG's results into one
                        answer. Bare flag uses the orchestrator model; with an
                        argument, that model instead.
  --max-concurrent MAX_CONCURRENT
                        Cap on agents running at the same time within one
                        phase. 0, the default, runs the whole phase at once —
                        lower it to stay under a provider's rate limit.
  --output {text,json}  Result format: 'text' (default) for reading, 'json'
                        for a machine-readable run.
  --save DIR            Directory to write each agent's output and the run's
                        artifacts into. Required by --background, which has
                        nowhere else to report.
  --team-mode [NAME]    Create a FRESH team for this flow (new UUID every
                        invocation). Bare flag uses 'flow' as the name.
  --team-attach NAME    Attach to a team by NAME — upsert semantics: load
                        existing team if found (preserving message history),
                        else create fresh. Mutually exclusive with --team-
                        mode.
  --team-max-rounds N   In team mode (reactive), how many extra wakeup rounds
                        the coordinator may run after all currently-running
                        workers signal done, to deliver unread teammate
                        messages before the run wraps up (default: 2).
  --dry-run             Plan the DAG but don't execute. Shows agents, deps,
                        and model resolution.
  --show-graph          Render DAG as matplotlib visualization. With --save,
                        saves PNG to save dir.
  --background          Run flow in background. Requires --save. Check output
                        in save dir.
  --bare                Ignore agent profiles — all workers use the CLI model
                        spec. Roles define behavioral focus only, no profile
                        system prompts.
  --workers M1,M2,...   Comma-separated worker model specs (assignment i uses
                        pool[i % len]). Overrides the per-role model while
                        KEEPING each role's profile/system prompt — unlike
                        --bare, which also drops profiles. Enables mixed-model
                        flows (cheap roles + expensive roles).
  --pack PATH           Path to a YAML routing pack. Provides per-role
                        model/effort when --workers is absent. --workers
                        overrides pack routing.
  --max-ops N, --max-agents N
                        Cap total ops (nodes in the planned DAG). 0 = no
                        shared ceiling; reactive spawns are capped at 20.
                        `--max-agents` is a deprecated alias — prefer `--max-
                        ops`.
  --reactive MODE       Who may grow the live DAG by emitting a SpawnRequest:
                        'all' (default — every worker), 'off' (flat batch DAG,
                        no spawning), or a comma-separated list of roles (e.g.
                        'critic,evaluator') that alone may spawn. Caps still
                        apply via --max-ops.
  --resume RUN_OR_SESSION_ID
                        Resume a checkpointed flow from a prior process (by
                        run id, or any session/invocation/play id backed by
                        one). Replays the persisted plan verbatim — no planner
                        call, no other flow flags read
                        (model/prompt/playbook/etc. all come from the
                        checkpoint). Distinct from `li o ctl resume`, which
                        un-pauses a still-running session.
  --allow-degraded-context
                        With --resume: proceed even when a pending op declared
                        inherit_context — it runs against an empty branch
                        instead of its predecessor's conversation history,
                        which resume does not restore. Without this flag such
                        ops refuse loudly, naming them.
  --mcp-config PATH     Read this MCP config and hand its servers to every
                        worker this run builds. By default the nearest
                        .mcp.json at or above the directory this command was
                        run in is used, so the workers' tools come from the
                        submission rather than from --cwd. The file is read
                        once, at startup.
  --no-mcp-config       Hand the workers no MCP servers, and say so
                        deliberately instead of arriving there by an empty
                        search.
  --yolo                Auto-approve the agent's tool calls, so an unattended
                        run is never left waiting.
  --bypass              Bypass all codex approvals and sandbox (for
                        cloud/codespace environments).
  --fast                Route codex requests through OpenAI's priority service
                        tier (lower latency; requires account eligibility).
                        Does not change model or reasoning effort.
  -v, --verbose         Stream the agent's output as it is produced instead of
                        printing only the final result, and silence the
                        progress lines that would interleave with it.
  --theme {light,dark}  Pick the colour scheme printed output is tuned for:
                        'light' or 'dark' terminal.
  --effort LEVEL        Override effort (overrides spec suffix). claude:
                        low|medium|high|xhigh|max. codex:
                        none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max|ultra
                        (max/ultra clamp per model support). gemini-
                        code/gemini-cli: folded into --model as
                        Low|Medium|High (Gemini 3.1 Pro has no Medium).
  --cwd DIR             Directory the agent's process runs in — the repo or
                        worktree it acts on. Defaults to the current
                        directory.
  --timeout SECONDS     Hard wall-clock timeout in seconds. When set, a
                        [DEADLINE] preamble is injected into the agent's
                        prompt so the agent knows its time budget and can pace
                        reasoning accordingly.
  --invocation ID       Parent invocation id (from `li invoke start`). Groups
                        this session under a skill orchestration record.
                        Optional.
  --project NAME        Explicit project name for this session. Overrides
                        auto-detection from .lionagi/config.toml or git
                        remote.
  --resume-on-timeout   Deprecated and ignored on this command: it is accepted
                        so existing invocations keep working, but nothing here
                        reads it and it will be removed in a future release.
                        Only `li agent` implements it.
  --notify CMD          Shell command template run once this run reaches its
                        terminal status. Overrides .lionagi/settings.yaml
                        notify.on_terminal. Substitutes {payload} (full JSON),
                        {status}, {invocation_id}.

usage: li orchestrate fanout [-h] [-a NAME] [-n NUM_WORKERS]
                             [--workers M1,M2,...] [--pack PATH]
                             [--max-concurrent MAX_CONCURRENT]
                             [--with-synthesis [MODEL]]
                             [--synthesis-prompt SYNTHESIS_PROMPT]
                             [--output {text,json}] [--save DIR]
                             [--team-mode [NAME]] [--mcp-config PATH]
                             [--no-mcp-config] [--yolo] [--bypass] [--fast]
                             [-v] [--theme {light,dark}] [--effort LEVEL]
                             [--cwd DIR] [--timeout SECONDS] [--invocation ID]
                             [--project NAME] [--resume-on-timeout]
                             [--notify CMD]
                             [[MODEL] PROMPT ...]

Orchestrator decomposes task into N agent requests, fans out to workers,
optionally synthesizes. Effort can be embedded in model spec:
claude/opus-4-7-high. Flags may appear anywhere relative to the positionals.

positional arguments:
  [MODEL] PROMPT        Orchestrator model spec (provider/model-effort)
                        followed by the task prompt. Model is also used as the
                        default worker model unless --workers is set; omit it
                        when -a/--agent provides one. A single positional is
                        treated as the prompt.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -a NAME, --agent NAME
                        Load orchestrator profile by name. Resolves
                        .lionagi/agents/<NAME>/<NAME>.md first, then
                        .lionagi/agents/<NAME>.md. Profile provides system
                        prompt, default model, effort, yolo. CLI flags and
                        positional model override profile settings.
  -n NUM_WORKERS, --num-workers NUM_WORKERS
                        Maximum assignments the orchestrator generates
                        (default 3). It may generate fewer if the task does
                        not divide that far, and --workers specs beyond this
                        cap go unused.
  --workers M1,M2,...   Comma-separated worker model specs, assigned round-
                        robin (each may carry an effort suffix). This is how
                        one fanout mixes cheap and expensive models across
                        workers.
  --pack PATH           Path to a YAML routing pack. Provides per-role
                        model/effort when --workers is absent. --workers
                        overrides pack routing.
  --max-concurrent MAX_CONCURRENT
                        Cap on workers running at the same time. 0, the
                        default, runs them all at once — lower it to stay
                        under a provider's rate limit.
  --with-synthesis [MODEL]
                        Run a final pass merging the workers' results into one
                        answer. Bare flag uses the orchestrator model; with an
                        argument, that model instead.
  --synthesis-prompt SYNTHESIS_PROMPT
                        What the merged answer should be — a ranked list, a
                        decision, a single patch. Implies synthesis.
  --output {text,json}  Result format: 'text' (default) for reading, 'json'
                        for a machine-readable run.
  --save DIR            Directory to write each worker's output and the run's
                        artifacts into. Without it they land in the run's own
                        artifacts directory.
  --team-mode [NAME]    Create a persistent team for this fanout. Workers get
                        team context and results are posted as team messages.
                        Bare flag uses 'fanout' as team name; with arg uses
                        that name.
  --mcp-config PATH     Read this MCP config and hand its servers to every
                        worker this run builds. By default the nearest
                        .mcp.json at or above the directory this command was
                        run in is used, so the workers' tools come from the
                        submission rather than from --cwd. The file is read
                        once, at startup.
  --no-mcp-config       Hand the workers no MCP servers, and say so
                        deliberately instead of arriving there by an empty
                        search.
  --yolo                Auto-approve the agent's tool calls, so an unattended
                        run is never left waiting.
  --bypass              Bypass all codex approvals and sandbox (for
                        cloud/codespace environments).
  --fast                Route codex requests through OpenAI's priority service
                        tier (lower latency; requires account eligibility).
                        Does not change model or reasoning effort.
  -v, --verbose         Stream the agent's output as it is produced instead of
                        printing only the final result, and silence the
                        progress lines that would interleave with it.
  --theme {light,dark}  Pick the colour scheme printed output is tuned for:
                        'light' or 'dark' terminal.
  --effort LEVEL        Override effort (overrides spec suffix). claude:
                        low|medium|high|xhigh|max. codex:
                        none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max|ultra
                        (max/ultra clamp per model support). gemini-
                        code/gemini-cli: folded into --model as
                        Low|Medium|High (Gemini 3.1 Pro has no Medium).
  --cwd DIR             Directory the agent's process runs in — the repo or
                        worktree it acts on. Defaults to the current
                        directory.
  --timeout SECONDS     Hard wall-clock timeout in seconds. When set, a
                        [DEADLINE] preamble is injected into the agent's
                        prompt so the agent knows its time budget and can pace
                        reasoning accordingly.
  --invocation ID       Parent invocation id (from `li invoke start`). Groups
                        this session under a skill orchestration record.
                        Optional.
  --project NAME        Explicit project name for this session. Overrides
                        auto-detection from .lionagi/config.toml or git
                        remote.
  --resume-on-timeout   Deprecated and ignored on this command: it is accepted
                        so existing invocations keep working, but nothing here
                        reads it and it will be removed in a future release.
                        Only `li agent` implements it.
  --notify CMD          Shell command template run once this run reaches its
                        terminal status. Overrides .lionagi/settings.yaml
                        notify.on_terminal. Substitutes {payload} (full JSON),
                        {status}, {invocation_id}.

usage: li schedule [-h]
                   {list,get,limits,create,validate,apply,export,enable,disable,delete,trigger,runs,run,status}
                   ...

Create, list, enable, disable, trigger, and delete schedules via the Studio
API (default http://127.0.0.1:8765). Set LIONAGI_STUDIO_URL to use a different
base URL.

positional arguments:
  {list,get,limits,create,validate,apply,export,enable,disable,delete,trigger,runs,run,status}
    list                List all schedules.
    get                 Show schedule details.
    limits              Show the global concurrent-fire cap and current in-
                        flight count.
    create              Create a new schedule.
    validate            Validate + statically resolve a ScheduleSet file (no
                        database writes).
    apply               Reconcile a ScheduleSet file into the database,
                        atomically.
    export              Convert schedules into a ScheduleSet document (never
                        writes the database).
    enable              Enable a schedule.
    disable             Disable a schedule.
    delete              Delete a schedule.
    trigger             Fire a schedule immediately.
    runs                List runs for a schedule.
    run                 Show one schedule run.
    status              "Did it work?" summary for a schedule.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
